record.paper_title: Some Open Problems Related to Creative Telescoping
record.original_question: Develop an algorithm that takes as input a multivariate hypergeometric term h in discrete variables k_1, k_2, ..., k_m and decides whether there exist hypergeometric terms g_1, g_2, ..., g_m such that h = Δ_1(g_1) + Δ_2(g_2) + ... + Δ_m(g_m), where Δ_i is the forward difference operator in k_i defined by Δ_i f(k_1, ..., k_i, ..., k_m) = f(k_1, ..., k_i + 1, ..., k_m) - f(k_1, ..., k_i, ..., k_m).

evidence.quote: Problem 5.1 Develop an algorithm which takes as input a multivariate hypergeometric term h in m discrete variables k1, k2, ··· , km, and decides whether there exist hypergeometric terms g1, g2, ··· , gm such that h = Δ1(g1)+Δ2(g2) + ··· + Δm(gm). Here, Δi is the forward difference operator with respect to the variable ki.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be a field of characteristic zero (for example $\mathbb{Q}$). A function $h(k_1,\dots,k_m)$ of $m$ discrete variables is called a (multivariate) hypergeometric term over $\mathbb{K}$ if, for every $i\in\{1,\dots,m\}$, the shift quotient
$$\frac{h(k_1,\dots,k_i+1,\dots,k_m)}{h(k_1,\dots,k_i,\dots,k_m)}$$
is a rational function in $k_1,\dots,k_m$ over $\mathbb{K}$. For each $i$, let $\Delta_i$ denote the forward difference operator with respect to $k_i$, defined by
$$\Delta_i f(k_1,\dots,k_i,\dots,k_m) = f(k_1,\dots,k_i+1,\dots,k_m) - f(k_1,\dots,k_i,\dots,k_m).$$
The term $h$ is called Gosper-summable in the multivariate sense if there exist hypergeometric terms $g_1,\dots,g_m$ such that
$$h \;=\; \Delta_1(g_1) + \Delta_2(g_2) + \cdots + \Delta_m(g_m).$$
Design an algorithm that, given as input a multivariate hypergeometric term $h(k_1,\dots,k_m)$ (specified by the rational functions giving its $m$ shift quotients together with sufficient initial data), decides in finitely many steps whether such hypergeometric terms $g_1,\dots,g_m$ exist, and constructs them explicitly when they do.
artifact.status_search_result: The multivariate Gosper-type summability problem for hypergeometric terms remains an active research area with only partial results. Gosper's algorithm completely settles the univariate case, but extending it to a full decision procedure in several discrete variables has been open since being raised by Andrews and Paule; only necessary conditions and special cases (bivariate, rational-function setting, mixed case) have been treated in subsequent work.

status_evidence.title: On the Summability Problem of Multivariate Rational Functions in the Mixed Case
status_evidence.snippet: extending these results to the multivariate setting was proposed as an intriguing problem by Andrews and Paule; initial progress provides some necessary conditions on the summability of bivariate hypergeometric terms.
status_evidence.claim: The multivariate hypergeometric summability decision problem remains a research frontier with only partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Gosper summability of rational multiples of hypergeometric terms
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work addresses summability of rational multiples of hypergeometric terms, indicating the multivariate decision problem is still being investigated.
status_evidence.claim: Recent papers continue to investigate restricted versions of the multivariate Gosper-summability problem.
